notes:
☠️ THIS FILE IS THE STRIP, AND UNTIL 2026-09-06 IT WAS NOT. The delivery beat in home-beats.json carried its OWN copy of these tiles and InstallsPanel read that copy, so this manifest was imported by nothing: editing it changed no pixel, and the studio's Installs strip editor was a control wired to nothing. Both now read here. If you add a beat that shows a strip, hand it a manifest, do not paste the list into the beat.
Every installation and delivery article's PHOTOGRAPHS, one or two frames each. THE FIRST TILE IS FIXED: it is the frame the beat led with and Jarich asked to keep it at the start. Places only, never names.
☠️ PHOTOGRAPHS ONLY. Nine tiles were removed because they were advertising, not evidence: the five p### files are designed cards (two proof of delivery panels with a QR code and an ORDER NOW button, two monthly price cards, one thank you card), the two install-2026 files are marketing collateral (a studio render still captioned Step 4, and a How We Install promo graphic), one v frame is overprinted with a Bound to Pangasinan title, and one is a screenshot of a map. The naming holds the rule: p### means a poster the design desk made, v### means a frame from real footage. Anything added later that carries overlaid selling text, a price, a render or a screenshot does not belong on this strip.
☠️ A PRICE IN THE FRAME IS A PRICE, WHOEVER PAINTED IT (Jarich, 2026-09-06). v020-1 was a real photograph of a real install and it still went, because the clinic's own banner behind the crew read GET YOUR DREAM DENTAL BRACES AT 40 PERCENT OFF, LOWEST DOWN PAYMENT, under their illuminated name. The rule is not about who made the artwork, it is about what a visitor reads on our home page. The same install is still on the strip through v020-2, which is the crew and the unit with no signage in shot. All 30 remaining tiles were checked for prices and offers; this was the only one.
EXTENDABLE: the strip reads any number of entries and re-times itself.
☠️ FIVE FRAMES ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT AND MUST NOT BE ADDED BACK AT TILE SIZE (ruled 2026-09-06). v033-8, v039-1, v039-2, v039-5 and v301-2 are 360 pixels wide at source with no larger copy anywhere. A tile on this strip renders up to 384 css px, which is 768 device px on a retina screen, so they would be served at less than half the resolution the tile needs and would sit visibly soft beside everything around them. They are documentary article photographs whose captions describe the exact frame, so they are never swapped for a lookalike and never upscaled. They keep their place IN the articles, where they render small; they only leave the large strips. The same five are listed in the machine readable `stripUnsafe` map on this file, keyed by filename, so a picker or a future builder can refuse them without parsing this paragraph. ☠️ NEITHER OF THESE TWO MANIFESTS IS GENERATED BY A SCRIPT: unlike crew-shots and training-media there is no builder to enforce the refusal, so the only guard is this key and whoever reads it.
☠️ tilePx IS THE DECISION NOW; THE stripUnsafe MAP BELOW IS DOCUMENTATION. tilePx is the largest CSS width a tile in this strip renders at, MEASURED on a production build at 1440 and at 390, not remembered: 288x216 css on a desktop (270x202 on a 390 phone). A file is too soft here when it cannot supply DPR 2 across that tile. The tiles are 4:3 with object-fit: cover and the source photographs are portrait, so the WIDTH is what binds: the image is scaled by max(tileW/w, tileH/h), which for a portrait source in a landscape box is tileW/w, and the test reduces to source width >= 2 x tilePx (576px here). Comparing against the source's LONG side instead gives the wrong answer on this strip.
